sentences.要留意的是：你自己不斷在變，對方需要的往往是不變的那一部分。: Keep in mind that you're always changing, while what they often need from you is the part that stays the same.
sentences.你做事擅長打破現狀、重整局面。: At work you're good at breaking the status quo and reorganising things.
sentences.要留意的是：你開得了頭，收尾往往要交給別人。: The catch: you can start things, but finishing them often falls to someone else.
sentences.你不接受「一向如此」這個理由，要說得通。: You don't accept "it's always been done this way"; it has to make sense.
sentences.要留意的是：你比多數人早離開既定的路，最好先想清楚要去哪裡。: Watch that you leave the set path earlier than most, so it's best to know where you're heading first.
sentences.你的住處常在調整：搬、改、換。: Your home is always changing: moving, remodelling, swapping.
sentences.要留意的是：你變動多，長期的歸屬感就比較薄。: The catch: with so much change, your long-term sense of belonging is thinner.
sentences.你的疲累是週期性的：一段極耗，短暫平靜，然後再起。: Your tiredness comes in cycles: a draining stretch, a short calm, then it starts again.
sentences.要留意的是：你拉長每次重來的週期，比減少強度更有用。: Keep in mind that spacing out each new start helps more than lowering the intensity.
sentences.你要有東西在變才安心，停滯比忙碌更難受。: You need something to be changing to feel at ease; standing still is harder than being busy.
sentences.要留意的是：你要分辨哪一次不安真的需要改，哪一次只是習慣了改。: The catch: you need to tell when restlessness really calls for change, and when it's just a habit of changing.
sentences.你處理錢敢下重注，也敢認賠出場。: With money you'll make a big bet, and you'll also cut your losses and walk away.
sentences.要留意的是：你的財務起伏比別人大，而起伏多半來自你的選擇。: Watch that your finances swing more than most, and the swings mostly come from your own choices.
sentences.你在外面開得出局面，把搬動當作重新開始。: Out in the world you can open things up, and you treat a move as a fresh start.
sentences.要留意的是：新局面開出來之後，維持的部分你未必接得住。: The catch: once the new situation is open, keeping it going isn't always something you can hold.
sentences.你在朋友之間自然被推到中心，大家尊重你、依賴你。: Among friends you're naturally pushed to the centre; people respect you and rely on you.
sentences.要留意的是：你給得出方向，未必給得出親近，深交因此不多。: Keep in mind that you can give direction more easily than closeness, so you have few deep friendships.
sentences.你在兄弟朋輩之間，不是帶頭，就是找一個可以倚靠的人。: Among your peers you either lead or find someone to lean on.
sentences.要留意的是：你和朋輩並肩合作，反而是最難維持的狀態。: The catch: working side by side as equals is, for you, the hardest arrangement to keep up.
sentences.你對自己要求高，事情擺在眼前就想接過來，而且要做得體面。: You hold yourself to a high standard. When something lands in front of you, you want to take it on — and do it properly.
sentences.要留意的是：沒有人幫手時，你容易獨力硬撐。: The catch: when no one steps in to help, you tend to carry it all alone.
sentences.你在感情裡界線清楚，對相處方式有明確的期待。: In love your boundaries are clear, and you have firm expectations of how things should be.
sentences.要留意的是：你退一步，不等於失去分寸。: Keep in mind that taking a step back doesn't mean losing your footing.
sentences.你帶後輩時習慣給標準，而不是給空間。: With those you bring up, you tend to give standards rather than space.
sentences.要留意的是：對方想走另一條路時，你給的壓力會特別大。: Watch that, when they want to take a different path, the pressure you put on them is especially heavy.
sentences.你做事先立標準再推進，最適合有分工的場合。: At work you set the standard first and then push forward; you do best where the work is divided up.
sentences.要留意的是：你單打獨鬥時，容易變成事必躬親。: The catch: working alone, you end up doing everything yourself.
sentences.你對長輩和上司客氣，但不盲從，心裡保留自己的意見。: You're courteous to elders and managers, but you don't follow blindly; you keep your own view.
sentences.要留意的是：你表面順從而心裡不同意時，最好找機會說出來。: Keep in mind that when you go along outwardly but disagree inside, it's best to find a chance to say so.
sentences.你對住處有自己的標準，寧可遲一點，也要安排成自己要的樣子。: You have your own standards for a home; you'd rather wait than settle for less than what you want.
sentences.要留意的是：你搬遷和安頓的心理成本，會比別人高。: The catch: moving and settling in cost you more, mentally, than they cost others.
sentences.你的疲累多半來自把事情攬上身，交出去又不放心。: Your tiredness mostly comes from taking things on yourself, and not feeling easy handing them over.
sentences.要留意的是：對你來說，分工比休息更能減輕負擔。: For you, sharing out the work lightens the load more than resting does.
sentences.你要事情擺得妥當才安心，連小事也放不下。: You only feel at ease once things are properly in order, and even small matters stay on your mind.
sentences.要留意的是：你留一件事不處理，比多做一件事更能讓你休息。: Keep in mind that leaving one thing undone will rest you more than doing one thing more.
sentences.你花錢講體面：該花的不省，不想讓人看見拮据。: You spend with an eye to appearances: you don't skimp where it matters, and you don't want anyone to see you short.
sentences.要留意的是：你維持某個水準，本身就是一項固定開支。: The catch: keeping up a certain standard is itself a fixed cost.
sentences.你出外時，有人同行就很順，孤身一人就容易拘謹。: Out in the world, things go smoothly when someone is with you; on your own you become more guarded.
sentences.要留意的是：在新環境裡，你要學會開口請人幫忙。: Watch that, somewhere new, you need to learn to ask for help.
sentences.你在群體裡是熱鬧的來源，認識的人多。: In a group you're where the life comes from, and you know a lot of people.
sentences.要留意的是：你把幾段關係留住，比認識更多人要緊。: Keep in mind that holding on to a few relationships matters more than meeting more people.
sentences.你交朋友快、聊得來，場面總是熱鬧。: You make friends quickly and easily, and things are always lively around you.
sentences.要留意的是：你真正交底的朋友不多，需要時未必找得到人。: The catch: you have few friends you truly confide in, so when you need someone, they may not be there.
sentences.你好奇心強、學得快，興趣鋪得很開。: You're curious and quick to learn, and your interests spread wide.
sentences.要留意的是：你想要的東西太多時，力氣會散在半途。: Watch that, when you want too many things, your energy scatters halfway.
sentences.你在感情初期投入極高，感受鮮明。: At the start of a relationship you throw yourself in and feel everything vividly.
sentences.要留意的是：你對新鮮的反應比別人強，要給這份驅力另找出口。: Keep in mind that you respond to novelty more strongly than most, so give that drive another outlet.
sentences.你帶後輩把好玩的東西帶給對方，啟發性強。: You bring the fun stuff to those you bring up, and you're very good at sparking their interest.
sentences.要留意的是：你的興趣一轉，帶著的事就容易停在半路。: The catch: once your interest moves on, what you were leading tends to stall halfway.
sentences.你做事靠興趣驅動，想做時效率極高。: At work you're driven by interest, and when you want to do something, you're extremely efficient.
sentences.要留意的是：你不想做時拖得厲害，這個落差比能力更影響結果。: Watch that, when you don't want to do something, you drag your feet badly, and that gap affects results more than ability does.
sentences.你對長輩和上司不硬碰，但也不太受約束。: You don't clash head-on with elders and managers, but you don't take much restraining either.
sentences.要留意的是：你先做後說，長輩往往最後一個知道。: Keep in mind that you act first and explain later, so your elders are often the last to know.
sentences.你把住處看成可能性，容易因為新機會而搬動。: You see a home as a set of possibilities, and you'll readily move for a new opportunity.
sentences.要留意的是：你不把任何地方當終點，安頓感就比較薄。: The catch: since nowhere is a final stop for you, your sense of being settled is thinner.
sentences.你的疲累來自同時開太多條線。: Your tiredness comes from running too many threads at once.
sentences.要留意的是：對你來說，收窄比放慢有效得多。: For you, narrowing down works far better than slowing down.
sentences.你要有一件正在期待的事，心才穩。: You need something to look forward to before you feel steady.
sentences.要留意的是：甚麼都不缺、甚麼都不想要的時候，你反而會空。: Keep in mind that when you lack nothing and want nothing, you feel empty.
sentences.你賺錢跟著機會走：看到就撲上去。: You make money by following opportunity: when you see one, you go for it.
sentences.要留意的是：你容易把賺到的再投進下一個想要的東西。: The catch: what you earn tends to go straight into the next thing you want.
sentences.你在外面比在家活躍，陌生環境反而放得開。: You're more active out in the world than at home, and more relaxed among strangers.
sentences.要留意的是：你換環境不一定解決問題，問題往往跟著一起搬。: Watch that a change of scene doesn't necessarily solve anything; the problem often moves with you.
sentences.你交遊不廣，不愛應酬，在工作上靠成績說話；和人合夥做生意要特別謹慎，獨立負責一塊: You don't move in wide circles or enjoy socialising, and at work you let your results speak. Be especially careful about going into business with partners; running your own piece of it usually suits you better.
sentences.你不愛聯誼和閒聊，真正的朋友多半是一起熬過項目、一起辛苦過的同事或同學，平時少見: You don't care for networking or small talk. Your real friends are mostly colleagues or classmates you've been through a hard project with — you rarely see them, but they come the moment you call.
sentences.你適合帶團隊、管項目，目標一定下就推到底；只是你習慣自己先衝，身邊的人未必跟得上: You're suited to leading teams and running projects, and once a goal is set you push it all the way. You do tend to charge ahead yourself, though, and the people around you can't always keep up.
sentences.你不必急著定下終身：先把自己的事業和節奏站穩，再進入長期關係會更合適；在一起之後: There's no need to rush into settling down. Getting your own work and rhythm steady before a long-term relationship will suit you better — and once you're together, remember to say what you're thinking.
sentences.你教孩子或帶新人，要求對方自己解決問題，很少手把手；在對方真正卡住時伸一把手，不: When you teach a child or train someone new, you expect them to solve problems themselves and rarely take them by the hand. Stepping in when they're truly stuck won't weaken their resilience.
sentences.你適合管理和開拓的崗位：帶團隊、開新市場、接手難搞的項目；你凡事親力親為，對下屬: You're suited to roles that manage and break new ground: leading a team, opening a new market, taking on a difficult project. You do everything yourself; with the people under you, remember to be generous as well as firm.
sentences.遇到不合理的上司，你不會服軟，也懶得解釋；在正式程序上多一點耐性，能讓你少走冤枉: Faced with an unreasonable manager, you won't back down and won't bother to explain. A little more patience with the formal process will save you some wasted effort.
sentences.你對住處要求不高，一張床、一個做事的地方就夠；忙起來可以住在公司附近，家只是休息: You don't ask much of a home: a bed and somewhere to work are enough. When you're busy you'll happily live near the office; home is just where you rest, and you belong to whatever you're working on.
sentences.你習慣帶著疲勞繼續衝，覺得休息是示弱；在日程表上預先排好休息日，像對待工作一樣認: You tend to keep going while tired, as though resting were a sign of weakness. Put rest days in your diary in advance, and treat them as seriously as work.
sentences.你喜歡忙，閒下來反而不自在，放長假時可能會自己找項目做；給自己安排有挑戰的運動或: You like being busy and feel uneasy when idle; on a long holiday you may well find yourself a project. A demanding sport or hobby will relax you more than lying around.
sentences.你賺錢靠自己開局，也喜歡把錢的決定權握在自己手上；替公司管預算、自己創業都合適，: You make money by starting things yourself, and you like keeping decisions about money in your own hands. Managing a budget or running your own business both suit you — but the risk is all yours, so keep a way out.
sentences.你在外面的時間往往比在家多：出差、跑項目、到處開局；你在外夠果斷，也記得偶爾停下: You often spend more time away than at home: travelling for work, chasing projects, starting things up. You're decisive out there; remember to stop now and then to check your direction.
sentences.你隨和好相處，容易交到朋友，和同事、下屬也相處融洽；分工和分配資源時，記得開口說: You're easy-going and easy to be around, you make friends readily, and you get on well with colleagues and the people under you. When work and resources are being shared out, remember to say what you want.
sentences.朋友聚會你很少缺席，卻很少做發起人；大家商量去哪裡吃飯，你多半說「都可以」。: You rarely miss a get-together with friends, but you rarely organise one. When everyone is deciding where to eat, you usually say "anywhere's fine".
sentences.和伴侶意見不合時，你多半說「算了」；小事這樣處理很好，但家務分工、錢怎樣用這些事: When you and your partner disagree, you usually say "never mind". That works well for small things, but housework and how money is spent only get harder to talk about the longer they're left.
sentences.你和孩子、後輩之間容易溝通，對方有心事也願意跟你說；只是該定的規矩，你要記得狠下: Children and younger people find you easy to talk to and will tell you what's on their minds. Just remember to harden your heart and set the rules that need setting.
sentences.你適合做讓人舒服、有美感的工作，例如設計、餐飲、旅遊、生活品牌；氣氛融洽的團隊，: You're suited to work that makes people comfortable and has an eye for beauty — design, food and drink, travel, lifestyle brands. A friendly team will get better results from you than a high-pressure sprint.
sentences.你和父母、上司的關係融洽，長輩和上司安排甚麼，你多半照做；覺得不合理時早一點說，: You get on well with your parents and managers, and you mostly do what they arrange. When something seems unreasonable, saying so early is better than holding it in until you snap.
sentences.你對家的要求是住得舒服：採光好、有一張好沙發、有一個可以窩著的角落；比起升值潛力: What you want from a home is comfort: good light, a good sofa, a corner to curl up in. You care more about how relaxed you feel the moment you walk in than about what the place might be worth one day.
sentences.讓你心煩的事，你常常先放著不處理，結果越積越多；每星期找一個時間把擱著的事清一清: Things that bother you often get put aside, and they pile up. Set aside a time each week to clear what you've been leaving, and you'll sleep better.
sentences.你很懂得享受生活：聽音樂、看劇、慢慢吃一頓飯就很滿足；太舒服的時候，記得給自己一: You know how to enjoy life: music, a good series, a long, slow meal are enough to make you happy. When things get too comfortable, give yourself a small goal so the days don't all run together.
sentences.你適合做讓人舒服、享受的行業，例如餐飲、旅遊、設計、生活用品；替自己定一個具體的: You're suited to industries built around comfort and enjoyment — food and drink, travel, design, homeware. Set yourself a concrete savings target, or the money will slowly drift away during the easy days.
sentences.你到了外地往往遇到願意幫你的人，旅行、外派都容易過得順心；在新地方安頓好了，也要: Wherever you go, you tend to meet people willing to help you, so travel and postings abroad usually go smoothly. Once you've settled somewhere new, ask yourself now and then whether you want to move on.
sentences.你交朋友很謹慎，不輕易交心，但交上了就很長久；同事和下屬放心把事情交給你，因為你: You're careful about friendship and don't open up easily, but once you do, it lasts. Colleagues and the people under you are happy to leave things with you, because you rarely let anything slip.
sentences.朋友搬家、辦喜事、出了狀況，常常找你幫忙收拾；你幫得穩妥，也要留意有些人只在有事: When friends move house, plan a wedding or run into trouble, they often come to you to help sort it out. You help well — but notice that some people only remember you when they need something.
sentences.在工作上，你最擅長把已有的局面管好、守穩；要你從零開創，或者站在最前面指揮一大群: At work you're best at keeping an existing operation well run and secure. Starting from scratch, or standing at the very front directing a crowd, is not where you're most comfortable.
sentences.你是家裡調和氣氛的人，記得對方的習慣，把日子安排妥當；遇到搬家、轉工作這類變動時: At home you're the one who keeps the peace, remembers your partner's habits and keeps daily life in order. When a move or a job change comes up, you'll be more anxious than your partner — saying so early is better than worrying alone.
sentences.你會為孩子或後輩先把條件準備好，學費、工具、退路都想到；有些難處，讓對方自己面對: You get things ready in advance for children and younger people: fees, equipment, a fallback, all thought of. Some difficulties, though, are better faced by them once on their own.
sentences.你適合接手已經有基礎的事業或團隊，把它管好、做穩，例如大機構、家族生意、成熟的部: You're suited to taking over an established business or team and running it well — a large organisation, a family business, a mature department. Steady, practical work suits you better than chasing the latest thing.
sentences.你在大機構裡待得住，文件和流程處理得穩妥；和上司意見不同時你習慣自己消化，偶爾說: You can stay the course in a big organisation and handle paperwork and procedure reliably. When you disagree with a manager you tend to keep it to yourself; say it now and then, and they may well take it on board.
sentences.你喜歡住得穩定，也傾向在同一間公司、同一個地方長期發展；搬家或轉工作對你是大事，: You like to live somewhere stable, and you tend to stay with the same company in the same place for a long time. Moving house or changing jobs is a big deal for you, and you think about it for a long time first — there's no need to blame yourself for being slow.
sentences.就算事情順利，你心裡也在預備最壞的情況；把保險、備用金、後備方案準備好，你反而能: Even when things are going well, part of you is preparing for the worst. With insurance, savings and a backup plan in place, you can actually relax.
sentences.你要有餘裕才放得鬆：帳戶裡有備用金、日程上有空檔、事情有後備方案；替自己預留一點: You can only relax with something in reserve: money in the bank, gaps in your diary, a plan B. Building a little extra room into your life will do more for you than an expensive holiday.
sentences.你用錢有計劃，收入進來先存起一份，其餘才花；你的長處不在賺快錢，而在把錢守住、慢: You plan your money: when income arrives, you put some aside first and spend the rest. Your strength isn't making money fast; it's holding on to it and letting it build.
sentences.你在外地的生活通常安穩，長期外派、移居比短期出差更適合你；給自己一段時間觀察環境: Life away from home is usually steady for you, and a long posting or a move suits you better than short trips. Give yourself time to get to know a place, and you'll grow more at ease the longer you stay.
sentences.在團隊裡你常常主持公道、替人善後，大家敬重你；只是在你面前別人不太敢放鬆，偶爾放: In a team you're often the one who keeps things fair and cleans up after others, and people respect you for it. But they don't quite dare relax around you; setting principles aside for a joke now and then will bring people closer.
sentences.朋友失業、分手、家裡出事，常常第一個打電話給你；你幫得上就幫，自己有煩惱時卻很少: When friends lose a job, break up or have trouble at home, you're often the first person they ring. You help whenever you can, yet you rarely speak up about your own worries.
sentences.在團隊裡，你常常是把關的人：看出哪裡不合規、哪裡對人不公平，而且會說出來；朋友有: In a team you're often the gatekeeper: you spot what breaks the rules or treats people unfairly, and you say so. When friends have a problem, you're often the first one they come to.
sentences.你在感情裡常常照顧對方的生活、工作甚至家人；偶爾把自己的煩惱交給伴侶，讓對方也有: In a relationship you often look after your partner's life, work and even family. Now and then, hand your own worries to them, and give them the chance to look after you.
sentences.你會替孩子或後輩擋掉不少風險，同時要求對方守住底線；小的跌碰，讓對方自己承擔，才: You shield children and younger people from a lot of risk, while expecting them to hold the line on what matters. Let them carry the small knocks themselves; that's how they learn.
sentences.你適合講原則、要有人負責把關的工作：審核、合規、教學、監督、專業服務；在變化快、: You're suited to principled work where someone has to guard the gate: auditing, compliance, teaching, oversight, professional services. In fast-changing places that reward cutting corners, you'll feel out of place.
sentences.開會時你不會為了場面好看而附和上司；和長輩的爭論多半是原則問題，先分清哪些值得爭: In meetings you won't agree with a manager just to keep things looking smooth. Your arguments with elders are mostly about principle; work out first which ones are worth having and which you can let go.
sentences.例如搬家時，你先想的是長輩上落方不方便、孩子上學遠不遠，自己喜歡的間隔反而排到最: When you move house, for example, your first thoughts are whether older relatives can manage the stairs and how far the children are from school; the layout you'd like comes last. If someone at home needs looking after, you quietly rearrange things around them.
sentences.別人的麻煩你接得太自然，自己的時間卻被一件件佔走；遇到不屬於你的事，試著說一句「: You take on other people's problems so naturally that your own time gets eaten up, one thing at a time. When something isn't yours, try saying "I can't help with this one".
sentences.比起物質享受，你更看重精神上的充實：閱讀、學習、做對的事；只要自己那一關過得去，: You value a full mind more than material comfort: reading, learning, doing the right thing. As long as you can live with yourself, you don't much mind coming off worse.
sentences.你適合做有管理、審核、把關性質的工作來賺錢，例如會計、合規、行政；比起做生意冒險: You're suited to earning a living through work that manages, checks and safeguards — accounting, compliance, administration. A steady income suits you better than taking risks in business.
sentences.你到外地讀書或工作，身邊常有肯照應你的前輩或上司；到了新環境，你也很快成為別人依: When you study or work away from home, there's often a senior colleague or manager willing to look out for you. In a new place you also quickly become someone others rely on — remember not to take everything on yourself.
sentences.你身邊的同事、下屬和朋友常常在換，認識的人很多，留得下來的不多；大家打聽消息時，: The colleagues, team members and friends around you change often; you know a lot of people, but few of them stay. When anyone wants to find something out, you're the first person they think of.
sentences.朋友吵架時，兩邊都會來找你訴苦；群組裡的大小事你往往最清楚，卻很少有人問你最近過: When friends fall out, both sides come to you to complain. You usually know more than anyone about what's going on in the group chat, yet few people ask how you've been.
sentences.工作卡在某個流程時，你會先換個做法、找另一個人問，或者調一調次序；學新軟件、新規: When work gets stuck at some step, you try a different approach, ask someone else, or change the order. You also pick up new software and new rules faster than the people around you.
sentences.約會的計劃、家裡的安排，你常常臨時改了又改；你覺得是在找更好的方案，對方卻可能覺: You often change date plans and household arrangements at the last minute, then change them again. To you it's finding a better option; your partner may feel they can't keep up.
sentences.教孩子或帶新人，你會教對方解題的思路和做事的竅門；一次只給一兩個方法，對方更容易: When you teach a child or train someone new, you teach them how to think through a problem and the tricks of getting things done. Give them one or two methods at a time, and they'll pick it up more easily.
sentences.你適合變化多的工作：項目制、顧問、策劃、需要常常應變的崗位；日日重複、流程固定的: You're suited to varied work: project-based roles, consultancy, planning, jobs that keep you adapting. A post where every day is the same and the process is fixed will make you restless fastest.
sentences.和父母或上司意見不同時，你不會正面頂撞，而是另想辦法把事辦成；真正重要的分歧，還: When you disagree with your parents or a manager, you don't confront them; you find another way to get things done. For the disagreements that really matter, though, find a chance to have it out properly once.
sentences.你搬家、換工作地點的次數，往往比身邊的人多；環境一久沒有變化，你就會想動，買了房: You tend to move house and change workplaces more often than the people around you. When nothing has changed for a while you want to move, and even if you buy a place, you may not stay in it for life.
sentences.放假時你的腦袋仍在想工作，睡前還在重播白天的對話；睡前把明天要做的事寫在紙上，比: On holiday your mind is still on work, and at bedtime you're replaying the day's conversations. Writing tomorrow's tasks on paper before bed will help more than counting sheep.
sentences.你興趣很多，腦子也停不下來：看書、看片、研究新東西，一樣接一樣；睡前把腦中的念頭: You have lots of interests and a mind that won't stop: books, films, looking into new things, one after another. Writing down what's in your head before bed will help you sleep a little better.
sentences.你適合靠腦力賺錢：策劃、分析、找市場空隙，或者同時接不同的項目；收入每個月未必一: You're suited to earning with your head: planning, analysis, finding gaps in the market, or juggling several projects at once. Your income may differ from month to month, so a cash reserve will give you a lot of peace of mind.
sentences.你適合到外地讀書、工作或長期出差，離開熟悉的地方反而更有發揮；新環境裡的規矩和人: You're suited to studying, working or spending long stretches away from home; you do more once you leave familiar ground. You quickly get the measure of the rules and people in a new place.
sentences.你身邊的同事、下屬和朋友大多對你忠誠；你是讓團隊運作順暢的人，只是你預先避免的問: Most of the colleagues, team members and friends around you are loyal to you. You're the one who keeps the team running smoothly — though the problems you head off in advance aren't always visible to anyone else.
sentences.朋友之間有矛盾時，你常常是兩邊傳話、找台階的人；群組裡有人吵起來，你會先把話題引: When friends fall out, you're often the one carrying messages between them and finding a way for both to back down. If an argument breaks out in the group chat, you're the first to change the subject.
sentences.你很受身邊的人影響：跟對了上司和團隊，你能把事情辦得漂亮；環境不對，也容易被拖著: You're strongly influenced by the people around you. With the right manager and team you do excellent work; in the wrong setting you're easily dragged along, so choosing who you work with matters a great deal.
sentences.你和伴侶適合一起做事：一起經營生意、一起規劃置業或旅行，你會把分工和規矩定得清清: You and a partner work well doing things together — running a business, planning a home or a trip. You set out who does what very clearly, and the partnership runs smoothly.
sentences.你會教孩子或新人做事的規矩和禮貌，示範得清清楚楚；遇到沒有標準答案的事，讓對方自: You teach children and newcomers how things are done and how to behave, and you show them clearly. When something has no set answer, let them try making the decision themselves.
sentences.在職場上，你做副手、執行者，或者一個部門、一個地區的負責人，往往比坐最高的位置更: At work you're often more at home as a deputy, as the one who executes, or as the head of a department or region, than in the very top seat. At the top, pressure and attacks arrive together.
sentences.你熟悉公司的程序，懂得在規矩裡把事情辦成：申請、審批、文件都做得周全；遇到規矩沒: You know your organisation's procedures and how to get things done within the rules: applications, approvals and paperwork are all handled thoroughly. When something isn't covered by the rules, you can try making the call yourself.
sentences.你對住處的環境很敏感：採光、噪音、鄰居、大廈管理，都會影響你住得安不安心；租房或: You're sensitive to your surroundings at home: light, noise, the neighbours and how the building is run all affect whether you feel at ease. When renting or buying, you go through the contract and the paperwork item by item.
sentences.同事的請求、親友的拜託，你很少說不，於是日程排得密密麻麻；每星期留一段不接受任何: You rarely say no to colleagues, friends or family, so your diary fills up completely. Keep one stretch of time each week for yourself, closed to any arrangements.
sentences.你的心情很受身邊的環境影響：工作秩序清楚、家裡整齊，你就安心；規矩突然改了、分工: Your mood depends a lot on your surroundings. When work is orderly and home is tidy, you're at ease; when rules suddenly change or no one is clear who does what, you get irritable.
sentences.你管錢像管一枚印章：帳目清楚、簽名前看清條款、按時交款；替家人或公司管帳，你是最: You look after money the way you'd look after an official seal: clear accounts, the small print read before you sign, payments made on time. When it comes to managing the books for family or work, you're the safest pair of hands.
sentences.你在外面容易接近有地位、有資源的人，出差、外派常常得到上司或前輩賞識；在新地方先: Out in the world you easily get close to people with standing and resources, and on trips and postings you often win the regard of managers and senior colleagues. Learn the rules of a new place first, and your good judgement will open doors for you.
sentences.你記得同事和朋友的近況，會在群組裡關心別人、替大家牽線；你做的這些別人未必看得見: You remember how colleagues and friends are doing, check in on people in the group chat and put people in touch. Others may not see what you do, so say so when you're tired.
sentences.你記得朋友的生日、口味和近況，會在對方低落時傳一個訊息；只是你失望時不會吵，只會: You remember friends' birthdays, tastes and news, and you'll send a message when they're low. But when you're disappointed you don't argue; you just slowly get in touch less.
sentences.你做事前習慣先盤算、先計劃，把各種可能想一遍才動手；要你即場決定，你寧可說一句「: Before you act, you like to weigh things up and plan, running through every possibility first. Asked to decide on the spot, you'd rather say "let me think about it".
sentences.你會記得伴侶的喜好，先把家裡的事安排好，在對方情緒不好時接住；你自己想要甚麼，卻: You remember what your partner likes, keep things at home in order, and catch them when they're low. What you want yourself, though, you often leave them to guess.
sentences.你會留意孩子或後輩的情緒和作息，多於成績；有些決定交給對方自己做，你在旁邊看著就: With children and younger people, you pay more attention to their moods and routines than to their marks. Some decisions can be left to them, with you simply watching nearby.
sentences.你適合做規劃、策劃、分析一類的工作，把方案想清楚是你最有價值的地方；要你在前線即: You're suited to planning and analysis; thinking a proposal through is where you add the most value. A front-line role where you have to decide on the spot will take a lot more out of you.
sentences.你對父母和上司表面順從，心裡保留自己的判斷；你們看似親近，其實隔了一段距離，偶爾: With your parents and managers you go along on the surface while keeping your own judgement. You seem close, but there's a distance between you; now and then, be the one to say what you really think.
sentences.你很在意家的感覺：安靜、私密、東西放在自己習慣的位置；租房或買房時，在不同時段親: How home feels matters a lot to you: quiet, private, things where you're used to them. When renting or buying, visiting in person at different times of day is more reliable than going by photos.
sentences.家裡的雜事、朋友的心事，你都默默接下來；累的時候直接說「今天我做不來」，比硬撐做: You quietly take on the chores at home and your friends' worries. When you're tired, simply saying "I can't do it today" will restore you more than forcing yourself to finish.
sentences.你需要安靜的時間：一個人看書、散步、聽音樂，把一天收起來的情緒放下；讓家人知道這: You need quiet time — reading, walking or listening to music on your own — to set down the feelings you've held in all day. Let your family know this time matters to you and isn't you pulling away from them.
sentences.你習慣小額、長期地儲錢：定期存款、按月供款、為某個目標開一個戶口；突如其來的大額: You tend to save small amounts over a long time: fixed deposits, monthly standing orders, an account opened for a particular goal. A sudden large expense is what unsettles you most, so an emergency fund matters.
sentences.你到新地方，會先找好住處、摸清附近的生活，再慢慢展開工作和社交；在外地做事，走合: In a new place you first find somewhere to live and get to know the area, then gradually build up work and a social life. Away from home, working with people suits you better than fighting them.
sentences.你的社交行程總是排得很滿，誰找你幫忙你都答應；每星期替自己留一晚不約人，重要的朋: Your social calendar is always full, and you say yes to anyone who asks for help. Keep one evening a week free of plans, and you'll actually see more of the friends who matter.
sentences.朋友聚會多半是你約的，飯局你也常常搶著付；別人請你幫忙引薦、介紹工作，你很少推辭: You're usually the one who organises get-togethers, and you're often first to grab the bill at dinner. When someone asks you for an introduction or a job lead, you rarely say no.
sentences.聚會冷場時，你多半是先開口的人；同事有難處，你會主動幫一把，事後也不太記著。: When a gathering goes quiet, you're usually the one who speaks first. When a colleague is struggling, you offer a hand without being asked, and you don't keep count afterwards.
sentences.你會替伴侶安排接送、訂位、處理家裡的雜事，卻很少說自己累了、想要甚麼；偶爾讓對方: You arrange lifts, book tables and handle the household chores for your partner, but rarely say that you're tired or what you want. Let them do something for you now and then, and the relationship will be more balanced.
sentences.你願意為孩子或後輩花時間、花錢，報興趣班、介紹機會都不吝嗇；讓對方自己碰一次壁，: You're generous with time and money for children and younger people, signing them up for classes and passing on opportunities. Letting them hit a wall once on their own is also a kind of giving.
sentences.你適合接觸面廣、需要對外的工作，例如公關、傳播、銷售、社會服務；一生換幾份工作不: You're suited to outward-facing work with a wide reach — PR, communications, sales, social services. Changing jobs several times in your life is nothing unusual, as long as each one puts you in front of people.
sentences.你對上司和長輩有話直說，認同的就全力配合；在會議上反對之前，先私下溝通一下，摩擦: You say what you think to managers and elders, and when you agree you back them fully. Before objecting in a meeting, have a word in private first; there'll be far less friction.
sentences.你住的地方和上班的地方都不容易長期固定：搬家、轉公司、換辦公室，都比別人多幾次；: Neither where you live nor where you work tends to stay fixed for long: you move house, change company and switch offices more often than most. Each time you settle, give yourself a little time to adjust.
sentences.你需要一段不用回訊息、不用見人的時間：關掉手機半天、一個人去走走，對你比多睡幾個: You need time when you don't have to answer messages or see anyone. Switching your phone off for half a day or going for a walk alone will restore you more than a few extra hours' sleep.
sentences.你的自尊心強，做了事希望被看見、被肯定；空閒時你寧願幫人、做義工、辦活動，也不想: You have a lot of pride and want what you do to be seen and recognised. In your free time you'd rather help people, volunteer or organise something than sit idle on your own.
sentences.你的收入往往跟著名聲和位置來：職銜升了、口碑建立了，錢才跟著來；請客、送禮、資助: Your income tends to follow your reputation and position: the title rises, the name gets made, and then the money comes. You're never stingy with treats, gifts or helping others out — remember to set some aside for yourself first.
sentences.你適合到外地進修、交流、累積資歷，在外面建立名聲；到外地做生意就要謹慎一點，你在: You're suited to studying, taking exchanges and building experience away from home, and making your name out there. Be more careful about doing business abroad, though; your strength away from home is reputation, not quick money.
sentences.開會時你常常是指出問題的人，一時會被覺得難搞，事後大家才發現你說得對；找對時機說: In meetings you're often the one who points out the problem; for a while you seem difficult, and only later does everyone realise you were right. Pick your moment, and your views will be better received.
sentences.你和朋友之間講道理多於講人情；和朋友合夥、一起借貸，容易因為話說得太直而傷了交情: With friends you go by reason more than by sentiment. Going into business or borrowing money with a friend can damage the friendship when your words are too blunt; keeping things at a respectful distance is safer.
sentences.開會時，你會追問別人沒有想清楚的地方；買東西前，你會把評價和條款看一遍，才放心下: In meetings you press on whatever others haven't thought through. Before buying anything, you read the reviews and the terms before you feel ready to decide.
sentences.伴侶說的話有含糊的地方，你會追問到底；你是想了解，對方聽起來卻像被質問，先說「我: When your partner says something vague, you keep asking until it's clear. You want to understand, but to them it sounds like an interrogation; saying "this matters to me" before you ask will go much better.
sentences.孩子或後輩交功課、交報告時，你一眼就看出問題；先說一句做得好的地方，再指出不足，: When a child or junior hands in homework or a report, you see the problems at a glance. Say what they did well first, then point out what's missing, and they'll listen better.
sentences.你適合靠說話和分析吃飯的工作：教學、法律、顧問、談判、媒體；要你不問就照做的職位: You're suited to earning a living by speaking and analysing: teaching, law, consultancy, negotiation, media. A role that expects you to do as you're told without asking questions will be hard for you.
sentences.上司交代的事，你會先問為甚麼；問得有道理是你的價值，先說明你是想把事做好，對方就: When a manager gives you a task, you ask why first. Asking good questions is part of your value; make it clear you want to do the job well, and they won't feel challenged.
sentences.租房、買房時，你會把合約、管理規則、維修責任逐條看清；條款說不清的地方，寧願多問: When renting or buying, you go through the contract, the building rules and who is responsible for repairs, item by item. Where the terms aren't clear, you'd rather ask a few more times before signing.
sentences.你常在事後反覆回想自己說錯了甚麼、訊息有沒有寫好；給自己定一個時限，想夠了就放下: You often go back over what you might have said wrong or whether a message came out right. Give yourself a time limit; when it's up, let it go.
sentences.沒弄清楚的事會一直在你心裡轉：一封未回的電郵、一句聽不明白的話；把問題寫下來，能: Anything unresolved keeps turning over in your mind: an unanswered email, a remark you didn't understand. Write the question down and ask it if you can; that works better than forcing yourself not to think about it.
sentences.你的收入靠說話和專業：教學、銷售、顧問、談判、寫作；多爭取表達的機會，你的價值才: Your income comes from words and expertise: teaching, sales, consultancy, negotiation, writing. Look for more chances to speak, and your value will be seen.
sentences.你在外地靠口才和專業打開局面：講解、銷售、談判；剛認識的人可能覺得你說話直，相處: Away from home, you make your way through words and expertise: explaining, selling, negotiating. People who've just met you may find you blunt; after a while, they come to trust you.
sentences.你交遊廣，但立場分明：認同你的人很快成為好友，不認同的就漸漸疏遠；在工作上偶爾留: You know a lot of people, but your position is clear: those who agree with you quickly become close friends, and those who don't gradually drift away. At work, leaving a little middle ground now and then will open more doors.
sentences.你和朋友之間，保持一點距離反而長久：少借錢、少合夥、不過問太多，交情可以很深，界: With friends, a little distance makes things last longer: lend less, go into business together less, ask fewer questions. A friendship can run deep and still have clear lines.
sentences.你對理念和是非有很強的熱情：看到不公平的事，你會想發聲；在意的興趣，你能鑽得很深: You feel strongly about ideas and about right and wrong; when you see something unfair, you want to speak out. You can go very deep into the interests you care about, further than the people around you can follow.
sentences.你對伴侶的回應很在意：訊息回得慢、答應的事忘了，你都會放在心上；你介意的地方，最: How your partner responds matters a lot to you: a slow reply or a forgotten promise stays with you. Whatever bothers you, it's best to tell them directly.
sentences.你和孩子或後輩的感情很深，就算意見不合、隔膜一段時間，最後也能互相體諒；你的期望: Your bond with children and younger people runs deep; even after a disagreement or a spell of distance, you come to understand each other in the end. Just don't let your expectations turn into pressure on them.
sentences.你適合有商業味道、講究形象的工作：市場推廣、品牌、銷售管理；你做事講氣派、講規格: You're suited to commercial, image-conscious work: marketing, branding, sales management. You do things with style and to a high specification — just pace yourself, so a strong start doesn't run out of steam.
sentences.公司的規定你會認真遵守，前提是你認同它；遇到講不通的規定，先了解背後的原因，再決: You'll follow company rules faithfully, as long as you agree with them. When a rule makes no sense, find out the reason behind it before deciding whether to fight it.
sentences.你對住處的格局和氛圍很講究，搬進去之前常常想改一改間隔、燈光和擺設；裝修的預算，: You're particular about the layout and feel of a home, and before moving in you often want to change the floor plan, the lighting and the furnishings. Set a ceiling on the renovation budget in advance.
sentences.一件小事就能讓你生氣或難過好幾天，比工作量更耗你的力氣；遇到讓你激動的事，先隔一: A small thing can leave you angry or upset for days, and that drains you more than your workload does. When something stirs you up, sleep on it before you respond.
sentences.你閒不下來，放假也想找點事做：學一門手藝、做一個作品、投入一項運動；手上有事可投: You can't sit still; even on holiday you want something to do — learning a craft, making something, getting into a sport. With something to throw yourself into, your mind is at its calmest.
sentences.你的收入多半要在競爭中爭取回來：搶生意、爭客戶、談條件；認定了一件事你肯投錢，投: Your income usually has to be won in competition: chasing business, winning clients, negotiating terms. Once you believe in something you'll put money in — decide beforehand the most you can afford to lose.
sentences.你離開出生的地方發展，往往比留在原地更放得開：外地的工作、新的城市，讓你擺脫舊有: You often do better away from where you were born than staying put; a job elsewhere or a new city frees you from old obligations. Just don't tie yourself up just as tightly all over again.
sentences.同事信任你，因為你說到做到；你很少花時間閒聊或照顧別人的情緒，工作上合作的人多，: Colleagues trust you because you do what you say. You spend little time on chat or on other people's feelings, so plenty of people work with you, but few ask you out after work.
sentences.和朋友一起做事時，對方遲到、交得不好，你會直接說出來；共事的朋友欣賞你可靠，純粹: When you do something with friends and they're late or deliver poorly, you tell them straight. Friends you work with appreciate how reliable you are; friends you just have fun with may find you too serious.
sentences.計劃一定下來，你就想立刻動手；排隊、等審批、開一個又一個的會，最容易讓你不耐煩。: Once a plan is set, you want to start straight away. Queues, waiting for approval and meeting after meeting are what try your patience most.
sentences.伴侶心情不好時，你第一個反應是想辦法解決：查資料、出錢、出主意；對方有時只是想你: When your partner is down, your first instinct is to fix it: look things up, pay for something, offer ideas. Sometimes they just want you to sit down and listen.
sentences.看到後輩做得慢，你忍不住自己接手做完；給對方多一點時間，下次對方就能自己完成。: When someone junior is slow, you can't help taking over and finishing it yourself. Give them a little more time, and next time they'll manage it on their own.
sentences.你適合財經、營運、工程這類講結果、講數字的工作；目標清楚、責任分明的崗位，最能發: You're suited to results-driven, numbers-driven work such as finance, operations and engineering. Roles with clear goals and clear responsibilities get the most out of your ability to deliver.
sentences.你和上司、長輩相處直來直往，覺得不對就說；遞交報告、處理文件時，多花一點時間在程: You're straightforward with managers and elders, and you say when you think something is wrong. Spending a little more time on procedure when you submit reports and paperwork will save you a lot of trouble.
sentences.買房或租房時，你看的是實用和划算：交通、面積、將來好不好轉手；看房時別只看數字，: When buying or renting, you look at practicality and value: transport, floor space, how easy it will be to sell on. Don't just look at the numbers when viewing; factor in how comfortable it will be to live there.
sentences.你習慣累了也撐著把事做完，直到撐不住才停；覺得開始累的時候就先休息一天，損耗會小: You tend to push on and finish things even when you're tired, stopping only when you can't go on. Take a day off as soon as you start to feel tired, and the toll will be much smaller.
sentences.你休息時也在想下一步：數字、計劃、進度；事情推到有結論你才睡得著，所以把大事拆成: Even when you rest, you're thinking about the next step: figures, plans, progress. You can only sleep once something reaches a conclusion, so break big jobs into small pieces and finish one each day.
sentences.你對數字敏感，也懂得以錢生錢：投資、做生意、自己做生意，都比單靠一份薪水更合你的: You have a feel for numbers and know how to make money work for you. Investing or running a business of your own suits your character better than relying on a salary alone.
sentences.每次出差、外派或搬到新城市，你都會很快忙起來，新項目、新目標一個接一個；忙碌讓你: Every time you travel for work, take a posting or move to a new city, you're soon busy, with one new project and target after another. Being busy energises you; remember to leave yourself some breathing space too.
sentences.你在團隊裡常常是帶頭改變的人，有人支持你，也有人被你衝撞過；推行新做法前，先和幾: In a team you're often the one leading change; some people back you and others have run up against you. Before introducing a new way of doing things, talk to a few key people first, and you'll meet far less resistance.
sentences.每轉一份工作、搬一次家，你身邊的朋友圈就換一批；多年後仍然聯絡的，通常是跟得上你: Each new job or new home brings a new circle of friends. The ones still in touch years later are usually the few who could keep up with your changes.
sentences.你對舊東西不太留戀：工作做膩了就想轉，家裡的擺設、做事的方法，也常常想換一套；每: You're not sentimental about the old. When a job goes stale you want to move on, and you often want to change the furniture at home or the way you do things. Each time, you're willing to pay a price for the change.
sentences.和伴侶吵架時，你傾向把問題一次攤開、推倒重來；對方可能需要慢一點的步伐，給彼此一: When you argue with your partner, you tend to lay everything out at once and start again from scratch. They may need a slower pace; giving each other time matters more than settling it in one go.
sentences.你鼓勵孩子或後輩走自己的路，對方另闢蹊徑，你只會高興；你自己經常在變，給對方一兩: You encourage children and younger people to go their own way, and you're only pleased when they strike out on a new path. You're always changing yourself, so give them one or two rules that stay the same; they'll feel more secure.
sentences.你在工作上的長處是開新東西：新產品、新技術、新市場；年年一樣的崗位留不住你，你會: Your strength at work is starting new things: new products, new technology, new markets. A role that's the same every year won't hold you; you'll go looking for change yourself.
sentences.「一向都是這樣做」說服不了你；你比身邊的人更早想離開既定的路，轉工作或自立門戶之: "It's always been done this way" doesn't convince you. You want to leave the set path sooner than the people around you; before changing jobs or going it alone, think the next step through.
sentences.你的家常常在變：搬家、改間隔、換家具，很少同一個樣子住太久；每次大改動之前，先算: Your home is always changing: moving, reworking the layout, new furniture, rarely the same for long. Before each big change, work out the time and money first, so you don't discover halfway that the cost is too high.
sentences.你的精力一陣一陣：投入一件事時日夜不停，之後又突然提不起勁；在兩次大轉變之間，給: Your energy comes in waves: day and night when you're absorbed in something, then suddenly nothing. Between two big changes, leave yourself a real gap.
sentences.你過一段時間就想改變：換髮型、換興趣、換生活節奏；想大改之前，先問自己是真的需要: Every so often you want a change: a new haircut, a new hobby, a new pace of life. Before a big change, ask yourself whether you really need it or are simply bored.
sentences.你不擅長精打細算，強項是開新的收入來源：副業、兼職、轉一條新的路；收入因此起伏較: Careful budgeting isn't your strong point; opening new sources of income is — a side business, part-time work, a new direction. Your income swings as a result, so keep a sum of money you never touch.
sentences.你到外地發展，要靠一門專門的技術或專業站穩腳；先把手藝練好再出發，比匆匆換地方更: To make your way away from home, you need a specialist skill or profession to stand on. Mastering your craft before you go is a surer bet than moving in a hurry.
sentences.在公司或朋友圈裡，大家常找你拿主意、做決定；尊重你的人多，能跟你說心事的人少，偶: At work and among friends, people often come to you for a decision. Many respect you, but few can tell you what's on their minds; now and then, invite one or two of them for a meal on their own.
sentences.和朋友一起辦活動或做生意時，你不是主導一切，就是乾脆全交給對方；兩個人平起平坐地: When you run an event or a business with a friend, you either take charge of everything or hand it all over. Discussing things as equals is what tires you most.
sentences.在公司裡，你常常是把爛攤子接過來、再收拾妥當的人；交到你手上的事，你要做到自己看: At work, you're often the one who takes over the mess and puts it right. Whatever is handed to you, you won't hand back until it meets your own standard.
sentences.你希望伴侶在你的朋友和家人面前得體，家裡的安排也要有一定的樣子；這些期待，最好在: You want your partner to make a good impression on your friends and family, and you want home to be run a certain way. Those expectations are best spelled out at the start.
sentences.帶新同事或教孩子功課時，你習慣定好標準，要求對方做到；對方有不同做法時，先聽聽對: When training a new colleague or helping a child with homework, you set a standard and expect it to be met. When they want to do it differently, hear their reasons first.
sentences.你適合獨當一面的崗位：部門主管、項目負責人，或者自己做生意；身邊有一個能分工的團: You're suited to roles where you stand on your own: head of a department, leader of a project, or running your own business. With a team you can share the work with, your standards can reach further.
sentences.你的父母或上司多半有權威、有主見；你表面客氣，心裡卻有自己的看法，意見不同時，找: Your parents or managers tend to be authoritative and opinionated. You're polite on the surface but keep your own view; when you disagree, find the right setting to say so properly.
sentences.比起長期租住，你更想有一個屬於自己的地方，也願意為此早作打算；房子要佈置成你要的: You'd rather have a place of your own than rent for the long term, and you're willing to plan early for it. Only once it's arranged the way you want do you feel truly settled.
sentences.工作一多，你寧願自己加班也不想交給別人；試著把一件事完整交出去，只看結果不管過程: When the work piles up, you'd rather stay late yourself than hand it to someone else. Try handing one task over completely, judging only the result and not the process; you'll feel much lighter.
sentences.你放假時也放不下未完成的事，家裡一件擺得不對的東西就會一直掛在心上；接受「差不多: Even on holiday you can't let go of unfinished business, and one thing out of place at home will stay on your mind. Accepting "good enough" will make life much easier.
sentences.你的收入通常不缺，但錢一來就容易花在維持生活水準上：衣著、請客、給家人的都不省；: You're rarely short of income, but money tends to go on keeping up your standard of living: clothes, treating people, giving to family, with no corners cut. A savings account with an automatic monthly transfer works better than relying on willpower.
sentences.出差、旅行或到新公司，有熟人同行或有人引介時，你表現得最好；一個人到陌生地方，先: On a work trip, on holiday or at a new company, you do best when someone you know is with you or someone has introduced you. Arriving somewhere strange alone, make a point of getting to know one or two people you can ask.
sentences.你的社交圈很熱鬧，飯局、聚會、活動都少不了你；場面上的朋友多，把其中幾段關係好好: Your social life is lively, and no dinner, party or event is complete without you. You have plenty of friends for occasions; nurturing a few of those relationships properly is worth more than meeting more people.
sentences.你的聯絡人很多，一起玩、一起吃的朋友隨叫隨到；真遇到難關時，能坐下來深談的，可能: You have lots of contacts, and friends to eat out and have fun with come the moment you call. When you hit real trouble, there may be only one or two you can sit down and talk to properly.
sentences.新的運動、新的餐廳、新的課程，你都想試一試；手機裡收藏了未看的東西，可能比已經看: New sports, new restaurants, new courses: you want to try them all. Your phone may hold more things saved for later than things you've actually read.
sentences.戀愛初期你熱情又有新意，約會的點子特別多；在一起久了，一起學新東西、去新地方旅行: Early in a relationship you're warm and inventive, full of ideas for dates. Once you've been together a while, learning something new or travelling somewhere new together will keep things fresh.
sentences.你會帶孩子或後輩去試新的興趣：樂器、運動、旅行；開了頭的事，陪對方多走一段，效果: You take children and younger people to try new interests: instruments, sports, travel. Stay with them a little longer on what they've started, and it will do them more good.
sentences.你的工作多半和消費、交際有關，例如銷售、餐飲、娛樂、活動策劃；很多機會是在飯局和: Your work is often connected with spending and socialising — sales, food and drink, entertainment, events. Many opportunities come up over dinners and at social occasions; choosing work you genuinely care about matters most.
sentences.你對公司規定不硬碰，但總能找到空隙把想做的事做成，事後才報告；重要的事先打個招呼: You don't fight company rules head-on, but you always find a gap to do what you want and report it afterwards. Giving people a heads-up on important things will save misunderstandings later.
sentences.你容易被漂亮的樓盤或公司門面吸引；買房、選公司時，多看實際條件，別被裝潢和宣傳帶: You're easily drawn in by an attractive development or a company's polished front. When buying a home or choosing an employer, look harder at the actual terms, and don't be carried away by decor and marketing.
sentences.你常常同時開好幾個項目、好幾樣興趣，結果每樣都做了一半；先做完一樣再開下一樣，你: You often start several projects and interests at once, and end up with all of them half-done. Finish one before starting the next, and you'll find you're far less tired.
sentences.你需要有一件在期待的事：下一次旅行、一場演唱會、一件想買的東西；享受可以盡興，也: You need something to look forward to: the next trip, a concert, something you want to buy. Enjoy it to the full, and remember to set yourself a limit.
sentences.你很會運用金錢，也捨得花在享受和社交上；錢一到手就想著下一樣要買的，把一部分收入: You know how to use money, and you don't mind spending it on enjoyment and socialising. As soon as it arrives, you're thinking of the next thing to buy, so putting part of your income somewhere hard to reach first is what helps most.
sentences.你在外面很吃得開，出差、旅行總有飯局和新朋友；應酬多了容易累，也別把換環境當成解: You do well out in the world; every work trip or holiday brings dinners and new friends. All that socialising can wear you out, and don't treat a change of scene as the only way out of your worries.
sentences.帝座落在自己的基調上，標準就直接架在自己身上。: With the imperial star in its own seat, the standard is set squarely on yourself.
sentences.《全書》形容其人「忠厚老成，謙恭耿直」——這是自我要求的樣子，不是地位。: The *Complete Book* describes such a person as "loyal, mature, modest and upright" — a picture of self-discipline, not of rank.
sentences.這很容易被誤讀為命好，實際上它描述的是一種不容易放鬆的姿態：事情擺在眼前就想接過: It's easy to mistake this for good fortune; what it actually describes is a stance that rarely relaxes: when something lands in front of you, you want to take it on, and once you have, you want to do it properly.
sentences.有人輔佐時這是主導；沒有人輔佐時，同一種姿態就變成獨力硬撐。: With support around you, this is leadership; without it, the same stance becomes carrying everything alone.
sentences.主導遇上平輩，是你在兄弟朋輩之間的張力所在。: The tension among your siblings and peers lies in a leader meeting equals.
sentences.《全書》記「紫微有倚靠年長之兄」，指向的是這段關係裡有一個位階感——不是你帶頭，: The *Complete Book* notes an "elder brother to lean on", which points to a sense of rank in these relationships: either you lead, or you look for someone to lean on.
sentences.平輩關係本該是平的，紫微卻習慣有上有下。: Relationships between equals should be level, but Zi Wei is used to someone above and someone below.
sentences.紫微和平輩合作時，容易變成一個人拿主意，或者反過來完全交出去，中間那種並肩的狀態: When you work with peers, it easily turns into one person making every call, or the opposite, handing everything over; standing side by side is the hardest state to keep up.
sentences.《全書》寫「晚聘諧老性剛」：你在感情裡有自己的分寸，不輕易遷就。: The *Complete Book* speaks of "a late match that lasts, with a firm temperament": in love you have your own sense of measure and don't easily give way.
sentences.紫微的標準感放進親密關係，會變成對相處方式有清楚的期待：什麼算體面、什麼算過分，: Brought into a close relationship, Zi Wei's sense of standards becomes clear expectations of how things should be: the lines between what's fitting and what's too much are drawn sharply.
sentences.紫微這份分寸使關係穩定，也使讓步變得困難——退一步在別的地方只是妥協，在這裡會被: That sense of measure keeps a relationship steady, and also makes giving way hard — a step back that elsewhere is just compromise feels, here, like losing your footing.
sentences.紫微對「培養」這件事的姿態：它傾向於給出標準，而不是給出空間。: When you bring others up, Zi Wei has you give them standards rather than space.
sentences.對後輩、學生或自己的作品，這個人容易把自己認定的好投射過去，要求對方達到。: With juniors, students or your own work, you tend to project your own idea of good onto them and expect it to be met.
sentences.結果往往是關係緊密而壓力偏高，尤其在對方想走另一條路的時候。: The result is usually a close relationship under high pressure, especially when they want to take a different path.
sentences.《全書》寫「紫微豐足倉箱」：你的錢通常夠用，穩而不多。: The *Complete Book* speaks of "full granaries": you usually have enough money, steady rather than plentiful.
sentences.紫微處理資源的方式偏向維持體面：該花的不省，不該讓人看見拮据的地方尤其不省。: Zi Wei has you handle money with an eye to appearances: you don't skimp where it matters, and especially not where being short would show.
sentences.它不擅長精算，也不太願意為小數目反覆計較。: You're not one for fine calculation, and you don't care to haggle over small sums.
sentences.這使收支通常過得去，但也使「維持某個水準」本身成為一項固定開支。: This usually keeps the books balanced, but it also makes "keeping up a certain standard" a fixed cost in itself.
sentences.《全書》寫「紫微災少」：你的消耗多半不來自大事。: The *Complete Book* says Zi Wei brings "few troubles": what wears you down rarely comes from big events.
sentences.紫微的消耗不來自事情多，而來自把事情攬上身之後不肯放手——標準在自己這裡，交出去: What wears you down isn't how much there is to do but taking things on and refusing to let go — the standard lives with you, so handing things over never feels safe.
sentences.紫微長期的疲勞多半是責任堆疊而成，而不是某一件大事造成。: Your long-term tiredness is mostly responsibilities stacking up, not one big thing.
sentences.鬆手比休息更能解決問題。: Letting go solves more than resting does.
sentences.對你的提醒是分工，不是休息。: The reminder for you is to share the work, not to rest.
sentences.《全書》記「紫微同左右出外貴人扶持發福」：你在外的表現，很看有沒有人同行。: The *Complete Book* notes that with its aides beside it, Zi Wei "meets helpful people away from home and prospers": how you do out in the world depends a great deal on whether someone is with you.
sentences.紫微在陌生場合不擅長主動求助，卻又習慣站在被看見的位置，於是有人引介時相當順利，: In unfamiliar settings Zi Wei isn't good at asking for help, yet it's used to being seen, so with an introduction things go smoothly, and alone you can seem stiff.
sentences.換環境對這個人不是難事，難的是在新環境裡承認自己需要幫忙。: Changing your surroundings isn't hard for you; admitting you need help somewhere new is.
sentences.外部條件對你的影響，大於它自身的強弱。: Outside conditions affect you more than the star's own strength does.
sentences.《全書》寫「紫微成行得力」，描述的是這個人在群體裡自然被推到中心。: The *Complete Book* says Zi Wei "gathers a capable following", describing someone a group naturally pushes to the centre.
sentences.你在朋友之間的張力在於：紫微給得出方向，卻不太給得出親近。: The tension in your friendships is that Zi Wei can give direction more easily than closeness.
sentences.旁人會尊重你、依賴你，但未必會跟你講心事。: People respect you and rely on you, but may not tell you what's on their minds.
sentences.紫微的人脈通常不薄，深交卻不多。: Your network is usually substantial, but deep friendships are few.
sentences.群體給你位置，未必給你親近，這個落差本身就是消耗。: A group gives you a position but not necessarily closeness, and that gap is a drain in itself.
sentences.《全書》說紫微在這裡喜「遇左右昌曲魁鉞」：身邊有得力的助手，你的標準才推得開。: The *Complete Book* says Zi Wei here is glad to "meet its aides and scholars": with capable helpers around you, your standards can reach further.
sentences.紫微的做事方式是先立標準再推進，適合有結構、有分工的場合；在需要單打獨鬥或事事親: Zi Wei has you set the standard first and then push forward, which suits structured settings where the work is shared; in roles where you must work alone and handle everything, the same approach turns into doing it all yourself.
sentences.《全書》寫「紫微茂盛自置旺相」：你傾向自己安排一個合心意的地方。: The *Complete Book* says Zi Wei "flourishes in a home of its own making": you tend to arrange a place that suits you yourself.
sentences.紫微對居所的態度是要合乎自己的標準，而不是有地方住就算——寧可遲一點、貴一點，也: Zi Wei has you want a home that meets your own standard, not just somewhere to live — later or dearer is fine, as long as it's arranged your way.
sentences.這使安置這件事被拖長，也使搬遷時的心理成本偏高。: This makes settling in a long process, and makes moving cost more, mentally.
sentences.歸屬感對你而言，是安排出來的，不是住出來的。: For you, belonging is something arranged, not something that grows from living somewhere.
sentences.《全書》寫「紫微福厚享福安樂」，但對你真正有用的是它的反面。: The *Complete Book* speaks of "deep blessings and comfortable ease", but what really helps you is the other side of it.
sentences.紫微的安定來自事情處在自己認可的狀態——整齊、說得過去、不失禮。: You find calm when things are in a state you approve of — tidy, defensible, nothing improper.
sentences.一旦某件事擺得不妥，即使無關緊要也會持續佔用心神。: Once something is out of place, it keeps taking up your attention, however unimportant it is.
sentences.所以這個人的精神消耗常常不在大事，而在收不了尾的小事。: So what drains you is often not the big things but the small ones you can't finish off.
sentences.能放著不管，對你而言是最有效的休息。: Being able to leave something alone is the most effective rest for you.
sentences.留一件事不處理，比多做一件事更難。: Leaving one thing undone is harder than doing one thing more.
sentences.紫微傾向於尊重制度，同時也傾向於認為自己的判斷同樣站得住——於是對長輩與上級多半: Zi Wei has you respect the system while trusting that your own judgement stands up just as well — so with elders and superiors you're mostly courteous but not blindly obedient.
sentences.表面順從、實際保留意見，是你和長輩常見的相處模式。: Going along outwardly while keeping your own view is how you usually deal with elders.
sentences.文書與正式程序上，你通常做得相當周到。: With paperwork and formal procedure, you're usually very thorough.
sentences.《全書》形容天府坐命「心性溫和」，而天府的溫和是有底的那種。: The *Complete Book* calls Tian Fu in the Life Palace "gentle in temperament", and Tian Fu's gentleness has solid ground underneath.
sentences.它的基調是先把底盤做穩再談其他：不冒進、不空手承諾、對風險的容忍度偏低。: Your keynote here is securing the foundations before anything else: no rushing ahead, no empty promises, and a low tolerance for risk.
sentences.這使你可靠，也使你在需要當機立斷的場合顯得慢半拍。: This makes you reliable, and also half a beat slow when a snap decision is needed.
sentences.與紫微的差別在於，紫微在意事情做得體面，天府在意事情不要出缺口——一個向前，一個: The difference from Zi Wei is that Zi Wei cares about doing things properly, while Tian Fu cares about leaving no gaps — one reaches forward, the other roots down.
sentences.穩與保守是同一種性質，處境不同評價就不同。: Steadiness and caution are the same quality, judged differently depending on the situation.
sentences.天府在平輩關係裡的位置：它是接得住的那一個。: Among your peers, Tian Fu makes you the one who can take the weight.
sentences.朋友有事會找你，而且多半是找你處理善後而不是出主意。: Friends come to you when something goes wrong, usually to help clear up rather than for ideas.
sentences.天府接得住，使你在群體裡的分量穩定累積，也使你承接的分量往往超出自己開口要求的。: Being able to take the weight builds your standing in a group steadily, and also means you often take on more than you were asked for.
sentences.長期下來，關係裡的付出與索取容易失衡，而你自己不太察覺。: Over time, the giving and taking in these relationships tips out of balance, and you hardly notice.
sentences.《全書》寫「天府相生寵愛」，天府把關係當作要守住的東西。: The *Complete Book* speaks of "mutual support and affection"; Tian Fu treats a relationship as something to protect.
sentences.它願意投入時間與安排，傾向於用穩定而不是激情去維持——記得對方的習慣、把日子安排: You're willing to give time and effort, and you keep things going through steadiness rather than passion — remembering habits, keeping daily life in order, stopping arguments from escalating.
sentences.相對地，它對變動的耐受度低，關係裡出現不確定時，反應往往是先收緊而不是先談開。: On the other hand, you have little tolerance for change, and when a relationship feels uncertain your reflex is to tighten your hold rather than talk.
sentences.天府對培養的態度：它給的是環境而不是要求。: When you bring others up, Tian Fu has you provide the right conditions rather than demands.
sentences.對後輩、學生或自己在做的事，這個人傾向於先把條件備齊——資源、餘裕、退路——再讓: With juniors, students or your own projects, you tend to get the conditions in place first — resources, slack, a way out — and then let things grow by themselves.
sentences.這種方式安全，但也可能過度保護，把本該由對方承擔的難處提前接了過來，使對方少了一: This is safe, but it can also overprotect, taking on in advance difficulties that were theirs to carry, and leaving them one less experience of holding up on their own.
sentences.《全書》寫「終身保守」：你一生用錢都偏向穩守。: The *Complete Book* says "cautious all your life": you lean towards keeping your money safe.
sentences.天府處理資源的核心是持有而不是流動：先留下安全邊際，再考慮動用。: Tian Fu has you hold money rather than move it: a safety margin first, spending later.
sentences.它不追高、不好賭、對來得太快的錢反而警覺。: You don't chase prices or gamble, and you're wary of money that comes too fast.
sentences.這使資源不容易大起大落，也使它較難抓住需要果斷投入的時機。: This keeps your finances from swinging wildly, and also makes it harder for you to seize moments that need a decisive commitment.
sentences.《全書》寫「天府災少臨災有救」：你的底子穩，消耗多半撐得住。: The *Complete Book* says Tian Fu brings "few troubles, and help when trouble comes": your foundations are steady, and you can usually bear what wears you down.
sentences.天府的消耗來自警覺：它習慣預先想好萬一，於是即使風平浪靜也在維持一份防備。: What wears you down is vigilance: you're in the habit of planning for the worst, so even in calm weather you stay on guard.
sentences.這種長期低度的緊張不劇烈，卻不容易間斷。: This long, low-level tension isn't intense, but it rarely lets up.
sentences.對你而言，真正的休息不是停下來，而是有一段時間確定不需要準備什麼。: For you, real rest isn't stopping; it's a stretch of time when you know there's nothing to prepare for.
sentences.有底比有閒更能讓你鬆下來。: Having something in reserve relaxes you more than having free time.
sentences.《全書》寫「天府出外遇貴人扶」，而實際的樣子是：天府在陌生環境裡不搶先，先觀察。: The *Complete Book* says Tian Fu "meets helpful people away from home"; in practice, it doesn't rush in somewhere new but watches first.
sentences.它適應得不快但適應得穩，通常在一段時間之後才開始發揮。: You adapt slowly but surely, and usually only start to shine after a while.
sentences.這使短期的場合對它不利——來不及鋪墊就要表現——而長期外派或長住則相當合適。: This puts you at a disadvantage in short-term situations — you have to perform before you've laid the groundwork — while long postings or long stays suit you well.
sentences.換言之，它的優勢在時間，不在臨場。: In other words, your strength shows over time, not on the spot.
sentences.《全書》寫「天府得力一呼百諾」，但更準確的描述是：天府在群體裡是被信任的那一個，: The *Complete Book* says Tian Fu "calls and a hundred answer", but more precisely, it's the one a group trusts rather than the one it follows.
sentences.旁人把事情交給你，因為知道不會出漏子。: People leave things with you because they know nothing will slip.
sentences.這使你累積的關係偏向可靠而非熱絡，圈子不大但流失率低。: So the relationships you build are reliable rather than warm, and your circle is small but rarely loses anyone.
sentences.圈子不大，但流失率低，長期算下來未必吃虧。: A small circle that rarely loses anyone isn't necessarily a bad deal over the long run.
sentences.天府的做事方式是把流程與資源先安排妥當，再開始推進——它擅長守住一攤已經存在的事: Tian Fu has you put processes and resources in order before moving forward — you're good at keeping an existing operation secure, and at turning a mess into something that runs.
sentences.相對地，從零開創、或者需要冒風險換取速度的位置，同一種方式會顯得保守。: By contrast, in roles that mean starting from scratch or taking risks for speed, the same approach looks cautious.
sentences.這是天府最順的位置之一：安置與歸屬本來就是它的本行。: This is one of Tian Fu's easiest positions: making a home and belonging somewhere come naturally to you.
sentences.這個人對住處與長期基地看得比多數人重，願意為此付出額外成本，也不容易輕率搬動。: You take home and a long-term base more seriously than most, you're willing to pay extra for it, and you don't move lightly.
sentences.要留意的反面是，一旦這個基地出現變數，你受到的擾動會比想像中大。: The other side to watch is that if that base is ever unsettled, it will shake you more than you'd expect.
sentences.《全書》寫「天府安靜享福」，你的安定條件相當具體：有餘裕。: The *Complete Book* speaks of "quiet enjoyment"; what you need to feel settled is specific: something in reserve.
sentences.天府需要知道還有多的——多的時間、多的錢、多一條路——才放鬆得下來。: You need to know there's more — more time, more money, one more way out — before you can relax.
sentences.剛剛好對它而言不是安全而是緊繃。: For you, just enough doesn't feel safe; it feels tight.
sentences.天府的精神狀態與實際處境的關係，往往不在於處境有多好，而在於邊際有多寬。: Your peace of mind depends less on how good things are than on how wide the margins are.
sentences.留白比享受更能讓它安定。: Empty space settles you more than pleasure does.
sentences.對你而言，留白本身就是一種收入。: For you, empty space is a kind of income in itself.
sentences.天府傾向於照章辦事，也傾向於維持關係的表面完整——有分歧多半自己消化，不輕易攤開: Tian Fu has you go by the rules and keep relationships intact on the surface — you mostly swallow disagreements rather than air them.
sentences.天府不輕易攤開分歧，使相處平順，也使真正的意見長期沒有被說出口。: Keeping disagreements to itself makes things run smoothly, and also leaves what it really thinks unsaid for a long time.
sentences.文書與制度上，你處理得穩妥，少有疏漏。: With paperwork and systems you're dependable, and little slips through.
sentences.你在制度裡待得住，因為制度提供的正是你要的那份確定。: You can stay inside a system, because a system gives you exactly the certainty you want.
sentences.太陽在命，基調是向外的：先照顧場面、先把事情擺上檯、先讓別人過得去。: With Tai Yang in the Life Palace, the keynote is turning outwards: looking after the room, putting things on the table, making sure everyone else is all right first.
sentences.《全書》寫「入廟形貌堂堂」：你一出場，旁人就感覺得到。: The *Complete Book* says that, when strong, it gives "an imposing presence": when you walk in, people notice.
sentences.太陽坐命最大的特點是廟陷落差極大——同樣一顆太陽，在午與在戌是兩種表現方式，一種: The defining feature of Tai Yang here is how much its strength varies — the same Sun in the Wu position and in the Xu position behaves in two different ways, one shining outwards, the other drawing in.
sentences.太陽在平輩關係裡的給予方式：它是出面的那一個，也是先掏出來的那一個。: Among your peers, Tai Yang makes you the one who steps forward and gives first.
sentences.朋友之間的飯局、引介、擔保，多半由你起頭。: Among friends, the dinners, introductions and vouching mostly start with you.
sentences.這使關係熱絡，也使付出與回收長期不對等——太陽不太擅長開口要求，於是給多了也不會: This keeps relationships warm, and also leaves giving and receiving out of balance for a long time — Tai Yang makes asking hard for you, so when you've given too much you say nothing.
sentences.失衡往往到很後期才被察覺。: The imbalance is often noticed only very late.
sentences.你的課題不是人緣，是記得替自己留一份。: Your task isn't popularity; it's remembering to keep some back for yourself.
sentences.太陽在親密關係裡的模式：它習慣用照顧代替表達。: In love, Tai Yang has you show feeling by taking care of things rather than saying it.
sentences.安排、打點、擋在前面，這些都做得自然；而把自己的需要說出口則相對困難。: Arranging, organising, standing in front come naturally to you; putting your own needs into words is harder.
sentences.太陽的關係裡容易出現一種不平衡——一方持續供給，另一方卻不清楚對方要什麼。: Your relationships tend towards one kind of imbalance: you keep providing, while your partner doesn't know what you want.
sentences.照顧得很好，卻沒有人知道你要什麼，是最常見的僵局。: Caring well while no one knows what you want is the most common deadlock.
sentences.太陽對培養的姿態：它給得多，而且給得明亮——願意花時間、給資源、替對方開路。: When you bring others up, Tai Yang has you give a lot, and give it brightly — your time, your resources, a path cleared ahead of them.
sentences.太陽這樣照顧人，使後輩受惠，也容易讓對方長期站在被照的位置上，較少自己摸索。: This kind of care benefits those you bring up, and can also keep them in the light for too long, with little chance to find their own way.
sentences.太陽落陷時，同樣的心意會表現為想給而給不出，於是轉成焦急或反覆叮囑。: When Tai Yang is weak, the same wish shows up as wanting to give and being unable to, which turns into anxiety or repeated instructions.
sentences.放手讓對方走一段彎路，對你而言是最難的一課。: Letting them take a wrong turn on their own is the hardest lesson for you.
sentences.《全書》寫「入廟豐足，陷宮勞碌不遂」，廟陷差異比多數位置明顯。: The *Complete Book* says "plentiful when strong, toiling without success when weak" — the difference is starker here than in most positions.
sentences.太陽處理資源的方式是流出而不是積存：請客、資助、投在別人身上，都做得毫不猶豫。: Tai Yang has you let money flow out rather than build up: treating people, helping them out, investing in others, without hesitation.
sentences.它不缺賺取的動力，缺的是留下的習慣。: You don't lack the drive to earn; you lack the habit of keeping.
sentences.廟旺時流出與流入大致相抵，落陷時則容易出多入少。: When it's strong, money out and money in roughly balance; when it's weak, more tends to go out than comes in.
sentences.留得住與賺得到，對你是兩件不同的事。: For you, keeping money and earning it are two different things.
sentences.太陽的耗損來自持續對外——要撐場面、要回應別人、要保持被看見的狀態。: What wears you down is always facing outwards — keeping things going, answering everyone, staying visible.
sentences.太陽的消耗不劇烈但不間斷，而且往往在別人看不見的時候才顯出來。: The drain isn't intense, but it's constant, and it often only shows when no one else is looking.
sentences.對你而言，真正的休息是有一段時間完全不需要對誰交代。: For you, real rest is a stretch of time when you answer to no one.
sentences.它的疲勞不在事情多，在沒有一刻是不用回應的。: Your tiredness isn't about having a lot to do; it's that there's never a moment when no response is needed.
sentences.《全書》寫「宜出外發福不耐靜守」：往外走對你有利，困在原地反而耗力。: The *Complete Book* says "prospers away from home, can't bear to sit still": going out into the world helps you, and being stuck in one place wears you out.
sentences.太陽在陌生環境反而更自在：有新的對象可照、有新的場面可撐，能量就有去處。: Tai Yang makes you more at ease somewhere new, not less: new people to look after and new occasions to carry give your energy somewhere to go.
sentences.留在熟悉而封閉的地方，同一股能量會轉成煩躁。: In a familiar, closed-in place, the same energy turns into restlessness.
sentences.所以你換環境的門檻低，成本也低。: So changing your surroundings is easy for you, and cheap.
sentences.熟悉而封閉的地方，對你反而最耗力。: Familiar, closed-in places are what wear you out most.
sentences.太陽在群體裡是發光的那一個，朋友多、場合多、被找的次數多。: Tai Yang makes you the one who shines in a group, with plenty of friends, occasions and calls.
sentences.太陽的課題不在人際不足，而在篩選——來者不拒使時間被切得很碎，而真正重要的關係反: Your task isn't a lack of people but choosing among them — saying yes to everyone cuts your time into fragments, and the relationships that really matter end up at the back of the queue.
sentences.它需要的不是更多關係，是把時間分給真正重要的那幾個。: What you need isn't more relationships but time given to the few that matter.
sentences.你的難處在於，拒絕對太陽而言比付出更費力。: The difficulty is that, for Tai Yang, saying no takes more effort than giving.
sentences.太陽的做事方式是站到前面去：對外、對人、可見度高的位置最合它用；需要長期埋頭、成: Tai Yang has you step out in front: outward-facing, people-facing, highly visible roles suit you best, while roles that mean keeping your head down for a long time with results no one sees will wear you away.
sentences.它擅長把事情推動起來，未必擅長把事情收尾。: You're good at getting things moving, less so at seeing them through.
sentences.它推得動，未必收得尾，這一點值得在安排分工時考慮。: You can push things forward but don't always finish them, which is worth bearing in mind when the work is shared out.
sentences.《全書》寫「入廟得祖業，初旺末平」：安頓的勢頭，前段比後段強。: The *Complete Book* says "inherits when strong; flourishing early, level later": your momentum in settling is stronger at the start than at the end.
sentences.太陽對居所的態度偏向開放：家是待客的地方，不是藏起來的地方。: Tai Yang has you keep an open house: home is a place to welcome people, not to hide.
sentences.它願意讓空間被使用，也不太計較被打擾。: You're happy for your space to be used, and don't much mind being disturbed.
sentences.相對地，它較少為長期持有做精算，安置的節奏多半跟著人走而不是跟著計畫走。: On the other hand, you rarely do the sums for long-term ownership, and how you settle tends to follow people rather than plans.
sentences.家對你而言是一個開放的場所，不是一個退守的角落。: For you, home is an open place, not a corner to retreat to.
sentences.你的安定不來自清閒，而來自有事可做、有人可顧。: You find calm not in having nothing to do, but in having something to do and someone to look after.
sentences.完全空下來時，太陽反而不安。: With nothing at all to do, Tai Yang leaves you uneasy rather than rested.
sentences.太陽的精神狀態與忙碌程度的關係，跟多數人相反：適度的負荷是它的地面。: With Tai Yang here, the link between busyness and peace of mind runs the opposite way from most people's: a reasonable load is what keeps you grounded.
sentences.真正令它耗損的不是事情多，是事情做了卻沒有人看見，或者對象根本不需要。: What really wears you down isn't having a lot to do; it's doing things no one sees, or for people who don't need them.
sentences.被需要，是你最實在的安定來源。: Being needed is your most solid source of calm.
sentences.太陽傾向於正面迎上——有話直說、該爭取的爭取、不太繞路。: Tai Yang has you meet things head-on — saying what you think, pushing for what you should, rarely going round the houses.
sentences.太陽有話直說，使關係清楚，也使摩擦來得直接。: Saying what it thinks keeps relationships clear, and makes friction direct.
sentences.它與制度的關係同樣如此：認同就全力配合，不認同就明白表示，中間地帶不多。: The same goes for how you deal with systems: full support when you agree, open objection when you don't, and little in between.
sentences.直接帶來清楚，也帶來摩擦，兩者同時存在。: Directness brings clarity and friction at the same time.
sentences.太陰在命，基調是往內收的：先觀察、先記住、先把感受放著。: With Tai Yin in the Life Palace, the keynote is turning inwards: watching first, remembering first, setting feelings aside for now.
sentences.《全書》寫「心性溫和，清秀耿直」，溫和之外還有耿直，這兩樣同時存在正是太陰坐命的: The *Complete Book* says "gentle in temperament, refined and upright" — gentleness alongside uprightness is exactly what Tai Yin gives you here: soft on the outside, with a firm measure of your own within.
sentences.與太陽一樣，太陰的廟陷落差極大，夜生與日生、坐在什麼宮位，會改變它是收得從容還是: Like Tai Yang, Tai Yin varies greatly in strength; whether you were born by night or by day, and which position it sits in, decide whether you draw in at ease or draw in tight.
sentences.外柔內有尺，是你最容易被低估的地方。: Soft outside with a firm measure inside — this is where you're most easily underestimated.
sentences.它不爭，但它記得，而且記得很久。: You don't fight, but you remember, and for a long time.
sentences.太陰在平輩關係裡的方式：它照料，但不宣告。: Among your peers, Tai Yin has you look after people without announcing it.
sentences.記得對方的事、在需要時出現、不邀功——這些做得自然。: Remembering what matters to others, turning up when needed, taking no credit — these come naturally.
sentences.太陰也期待對方同樣細心，而這種期待通常不會說出口。: You also expect the same care in return, and that expectation usually goes unspoken.
sentences.於是關係深而穩，一旦感覺沒被看見，退開也會退得安靜，對方往往不知道發生了什麼。: So relationships run deep and steady, and when it feels unseen it withdraws quietly, often without the other person knowing what happened.
sentences.它退開得安靜，所以對方通常不知道自己做錯了什麼。: You withdraw so quietly that the other person usually doesn't know what they did wrong.
sentences.相處方式上，太陰以維持為主——把日常安排妥當、把情緒接住、把衝突提前化開。: In a relationship, Tai Yin is mostly about keeping things going — keeping daily life in order, catching emotions, defusing conflict before it starts.
sentences.它擅長讓關係運作，較不擅長把需求說明白。: You're good at making a relationship work, less good at saying what you need.
sentences.所以常見的困境不是關係差，而是一方持續付出而另一方不知道有欠。: So the usual difficulty isn't a bad relationship; it's one side giving and giving while the other doesn't know anything is owed.
sentences.說出口，對你而言比多做一件事更有用。: For you, saying it out loud is worth more than doing one more thing.
sentences.太陰對培養的姿態：它照顧細節，注意對方的狀態多於對方的成績。: When you bring others up, Tai Yin has you look after the details and watch how they are rather than how they score.
sentences.太陰照顧細節，讓被照顧的一方感到安全，也容易變成過度貼近——替對方預先想好，反而: This makes those cared for feel safe, and can also become too close — thinking things through for them in advance leaves them fewer chances to judge for themselves.
sentences.太陰落陷時，同樣的細心會轉成憂慮，表現為反覆確認而不是放手。: When Tai Yin is weak, the same attentiveness turns into worry, showing up as checking again and again rather than letting go.
sentences.多留一點不確定給對方，反而是你最需要練習的事。: Leaving them a little more uncertainty is what you most need to practise.
sentences.《全書》寫「入廟富足倉箱，陷宮成敗不聚」，核心在聚與不聚。: The *Complete Book* says "full granaries when strong; when weak, gains and losses that don't add up" — the heart of it is whether money gathers or not.
sentences.太陰處理資源的方式是慢慢積：小額、長期、不聲張，而且傾向於留給具體的用途而不是泛: Tai Yin has you build up slowly: small amounts, over a long time, without fuss, and usually for a specific purpose rather than general saving.
sentences.它對開銷敏感，對突然的支出尤其不安。: You're sensitive to spending, and especially uneasy about sudden expenses.
sentences.廟旺時積得住，落陷時同樣的用力會變成反覆。: When it's strong, the savings hold; when it's weak, the same effort turns into going back and forth.
sentences.它怕的不是少，是突然。: What you fear isn't too little; it's the sudden.
sentences.太陰的耗損來自承接——把別人的情緒、家裡的雜務、沒人處理的細節一一收起來。: What wears you down is absorbing — other people's feelings, household chores, details no one else deals with, gathered up one by one.
sentences.這種消耗隱形，因為每一件都很小，而且多半沒有人知道是你在做。: The drain is invisible, because each thing is small and usually no one knows you're the one doing it.
sentences.對你而言，說出來比做完更能減輕負荷。: For you, saying it out loud lightens the load more than finishing does.
sentences.每一件都很小，加起來卻沒有一刻是空的——這是你的實際處境。: Each thing is small, yet together they leave no moment free — that's your real situation.
sentences.太陰在陌生環境的方式是先安頓再展開：找到住處、摸清節奏、建立幾個熟悉的點，之後才: Somewhere new, Tai Yin has you settle in before opening out: finding a home, learning the rhythm, building a few familiar points, and only then really starting.
sentences.它不適合頻繁移動，因為每一次都要重來一遍這個過程。: Frequent moves don't suit you, because each one means going through the whole process again.
sentences.相對地，一旦安頓下來，它在異地累積的東西往往比原地更多。: On the other hand, once settled, you often build up more away from home than you did at home.
sentences.每一次移動都要重來一次安頓的過程，所以頻繁變動對它特別不划算。: Every move means settling in all over again, so frequent change costs you more than most.
sentences.太陰在群體裡是維繫的那一個：記得誰的近況、把人和人接上、在別人沒開口時先遞一句。: Tai Yin makes you the one who keeps a group connected: remembering how everyone is, putting people in touch, offering a word before anyone asks.
sentences.太陰把人接上，使關係網細密而持久，卻也使它承接了大量不被記錄的情緒工作。: Putting people in touch gives you a dense, lasting network, and also leaves you carrying a great deal of unrecorded emotional work.
sentences.它很少主動索取，於是付出往往被當成理所當然。: You rarely ask for anything, so what you give is often taken for granted.
sentences.情緒工作不被記錄，也就不被承認，這是它最常見的委屈。: Emotional work that goes unrecorded also goes unacknowledged, and that's your most common grievance.
sentences.太陰的做事方式是把底層打理妥當——資料、流程、關係、細節，長期累積而不張揚。: Tai Yin has you keep the groundwork in order — data, processes, relationships, details — building up quietly over the long term.
sentences.太陰打理底層，在需要穩定積累的位置上很有力；在需要快速表態或對外爭取的位置上則容: Looking after the groundwork makes you strong in roles that need steady accumulation, and easily passed over in roles that call for quick statements or pushing your case.
sentences.它的成果通常要一段時間之後才看得出來。: Your results usually only show after a while.
sentences.《全書》寫「太陰入廟田多」，而太陰本就是田宅主，這是它最順的一格。: The *Complete Book* says "strong Tai Yin, plenty of land", and Tai Yin is the natural ruler of home and property, so this is where it serves you best.
sentences.這個人對住處有明確的要求，不是大小而是感覺——安靜、可控、屬於自己。: You have clear demands of a home, not about size but about feel — quiet, under your control, your own.
sentences.你願意花很多力氣把空間弄成想要的樣子，也會因為住得不對而長期不舒服卻說不出原因。: You'll put a lot of effort into making a space what you want, and in the wrong home you'll feel uneasy for a long time without being able to say why.
sentences.住得不對會影響它很久，而且它多半說不清楚原因。: The wrong home affects you for a long time, and you usually can't say why.
sentences.《全書》寫「入廟享福快樂」，但你的安定條件很具體：需要獨處。: The *Complete Book* says "when strong, enjoys blessings and happiness", but what you need to feel settled is specific: time alone.
sentences.缺了這段時間，即使外在順利，內裡也會持續積壓。: Without that time, even if things are going well outside, the pressure keeps building inside.
sentences.所以它的精神狀態與社交量成反比。: So your peace of mind runs in inverse proportion to how much socialising you do.
sentences.身邊的人常把這種需要誤讀為疏遠，其實只是它要的那段時間還沒有出現。: The people around you often mistake this need for distance, when really the time you need simply hasn't come yet.
sentences.留白對它不是奢侈，是必要。: Empty space isn't a luxury for you; it's a necessity.
sentences.太陰傾向於順著來——不正面衝突、不公開反對、把不同意見放在心裡慢慢處理。: Tai Yin has you go along with things — no open conflict, no public objection, disagreements kept inside and worked through slowly.
sentences.太陰順著來，使關係表面和睦，也使真正的距離不容易被察覺。: Going along keeps relationships peaceful on the surface, and keeps the real distance hard to see.
sentences.它對規則的態度同樣如此：照做，但保留自己的判斷。: The same goes for rules: you follow them, but keep your own judgement.
sentences.照做但保留判斷，於是關係看起來近，實際的距離未必短。: Following while keeping your own judgement means relationships look close, though the real distance may not be small.
sentences.太陰和長輩之間的疏離，往往沒有任何徵兆。: Distance between you and your elders often comes with no warning at all.
sentences.《全書》寫「性剛果決，心直無毒」：你剛而不陰險，只是直接。: The *Complete Book* says "firm and decisive, straightforward and without malice": you're tough but not underhand, simply direct.
sentences.長處是事情會被真的做完，代價是過程中的人與細節容易被輾過。: The strength is that things really do get done; the cost is that people and details along the way can get flattened.
sentences.與紫微的分別在於，紫微在意做得體面，武曲在意做完；一個看樣子，一個看結果。: The difference from Zi Wei is that Zi Wei cares about doing things properly, Wu Qu about getting them done; one looks at how it looks, the other at the result.
sentences.這種直接在共事時是效率，在私交裡是傷害。: That directness is efficiency at work and hurt in a friendship.
sentences.武曲的平輩關係往往極好或極僵，中間地帶很窄。: With Wu Qu here, your relationships with peers tend to be excellent or deadlocked, with little middle ground.
sentences.它把共事的尺搬進交情，於是關係不是極好就是極僵，中間地帶很窄。: You carry the measures of work into friendship, so relationships are either excellent or deadlocked, with little in between.
sentences.武曲在親密關係裡的方式：它用做事表達在意——解決問題、承擔開支、把麻煩擋掉。: In love, Wu Qu has you show care by doing — solving problems, covering costs, keeping trouble away.
sentences.武曲對情緒上的靠近，既不擅長也不太認為必要。: Emotional closeness doesn't come easily to you, and you're not convinced it's necessary.
sentences.於是關係裡常見的落差是：一方覺得自己付出了很多，另一方覺得沒有被理解，而兩邊說的: So the usual gap is that one side feels it has given a great deal, the other feels misunderstood, and both are right.
sentences.問題不在誰付出得少，在兩種語言沒有翻譯。: The problem isn't who gives less; it's two languages with no translation between them.
sentences.武曲對培養的方式：它給標準也給資源，但不太給耐性。: When you bring others up, Wu Qu has you give standards and resources, but not much patience.
sentences.對後輩或自己在做的事，它期待對方跟得上節奏，跟不上時傾向於直接接手而不是等。: With juniors or your own projects, you expect them to keep pace, and when they can't, you tend to take over rather than wait.
